WHAT THE NUMBERS LEAVE OUT

Confidence can hide a blind spot.

A unanimous neighbor vote can still be wrong. Compare the familiar training examples with the separate test set.

Where did the model get confused?

Rows are the known labels; columns are the model's predictions. The 16 synthetic test examples are fixed and are never used to fit the model.

This set is intentionally small and designed to reveal missing coverage. Once you inspect it and tune your data, it becomes development evidence. A real project needs a fresh, untouched final test set.

FIELD NOTES

Less “AI said so.”
More “let’s look closer.”

Signal Garden uses a real, small machine learning method: k-nearest neighbors. Fitting stores your labeled examples. Prediction finds the nearest examples in two-dimensional space and takes a majority vote.

There is no hidden language model, API call or paid service. Everything is computed in this browser using Euclidean distance. The vote share measures agreement between neighbors; it is not a calibrated probability.

01 / REPRESENTATION

A lot of agreement.
Very little coverage.

If all the examples come from the same corners, a model may learn the wrong shortcut. Look at where your evidence is missing.

02 / EVALUATION

Keep some evidence
out of the lesson.

Separate testing reveals errors a training score can hide. Repeatedly tuning against the same test set changes what that score means.

03 / HUMILITY

A teaching garden,
not a field study.

All seedlings and labels are synthetic. These scores demonstrate this exercise only. They do not establish real-world accuracy or learning outcomes.
